source_text: וַ/יֹּ֥אמֶר קַ֖יִן אֶל הֶ֣בֶל אָחִ֑י/ו וַֽ/יְהִי֙ בִּ/הְיוֹתָ֣/ם בַּ/שָּׂדֶ֔ה וַ/יָּ֥קָם קַ֛יִן אֶל הֶ֥בֶל אָחִ֖י/ו וַ/יַּהַרְגֵֽ/הוּ־־׃
english_snapshot: And Cain said to Abel his brother[a]. Then, while they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him.

signals.text: The Masoretic Text and the Judean Desert Hebrew manuscript 4QGenb (4Q2) move directly from 'And Cain said to Abel his brother' to the scene in the field, without recording Cain's words. The Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, and Vulgate preserve a clause equivalent to, 'Let us go out to the field.'

source_text: וַ/יִּוָּלֵ֤ד לַֽ/חֲנוֹךְ֙ אֶת עִירָ֔ד וְ/עִירָ֕ד יָלַ֖ד אֶת מְחֽוּיָאֵ֑ל וּ/מְחִיּיָאֵ֗ל יָלַד֙ אֶת מְת֣וּשָׁאֵ֔ל וּ/מְתוּשָׁאֵ֖ל יָלַ֥ד אֶת לָֽמֶךְ־־־־׃
english_snapshot: To Hanok was born Irad[a], and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.

signals.text: Hebrew has two spellings of the same name in this verse: Mehujael and Mehijael.

english_snapshot: And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz[a], Riphath, and Togarmah.

source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֥י יָוָ֖ן אֱלִישָׁ֣ה וְ/תַרְשִׁ֑ישׁ כִּתִּ֖ים וְ/דֹדָנִֽים׃
english_snapshot: And the sons of Javan: Elishah[a], Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

signals.text: Some manuscripts and 1 Chronicles 1:7 read 'Rodanim' instead of 'Dodanim.'

source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֖י אֲרָ֑ם ע֥וּץ וְ/ח֖וּל וְ/גֶ֥תֶר וָ/מַֽשׁ׃
english_snapshot: The sons of Aram: Uz[a], Hul, Gether, and Mash.

source_text: כָּל אֵ֨לֶּה֙ חָֽבְר֔וּ אֶל עֵ֖מֶק הַ/שִּׂדִּ֑ים ה֖וּא יָ֥ם הַ/מֶּֽלַח־־׃
english_snapshot: All these joined together in the Valley of Siddim (that is[a], the Salt Sea).

signals.text: Or, by later name, the Dead Sea.

source_text: וַ/יִּפְנ֤וּ מִ/שָּׁם֙ הָֽ/אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַ/יֵּלְכ֖וּ סְדֹ֑מָ/ה וְ/אַ֨בְרָהָ֔ם עוֹדֶ֥/נּוּ עֹמֵ֖ד לִ/פְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
english_snapshot: Then the men turned from there and went toward Sodom[a], but Abraham still stood before Yahweh.

signals.text: Some ancient witnesses read 'and the LORD still stood before Abraham.' The Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'and Abraham still stood before the LORD.'

english_snapshot: Esau ran to meet him[a], embraced him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and they wept.

signals.text: The verb translated 'kissed him' is marked unusually in the Masoretic Text with dots over the word. Some interpreters take this as signaling doubt or emphasis, but the plain sense of the Hebrew here is 'kissed him.'

source_text: וַ/יִּקַּ֣ח עֵשָׂ֡ו אֶת נָ֠שָׁי/ו וְ/אֶת בָּנָ֣י/ו וְ/אֶת בְּנֹתָי/ו֮ וְ/אֶת כָּל נַפְשׁ֣וֹת בֵּית/וֹ֒ וְ/אֶת מִקְנֵ֣/הוּ וְ/אֶת כָּל בְּהֶמְתּ֗/וֹ וְ/אֵת֙ כָּל קִנְיָנ֔/וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָכַ֖שׁ בְּ/אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וַ/יֵּ֣לֶךְ אֶל אֶ֔רֶץ מִ/פְּנֵ֖י יַעֲקֹ֥ב אָחִֽי/ו־־־־־־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: And Esau took his wives[a], his sons, his daughters, and all the persons of his household, along with his livestock, all his animals, and all his possessions that he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and went to a land because of his brother Jacob.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'to a land.' Some manuscripts and ancient versions support 'to the land of Seir'; many English translations render the phrase contextually as 'to another land.'

source_text: וַ/יִּהְי֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י אֱלִיפָ֑ז תֵּימָ֣ן אוֹמָ֔ר צְפ֥וֹ וְ/גַעְתָּ֖ם וּ/קְנַֽז׃
english_snapshot: And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman[a], Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.

signals.text: Some English versions read 'Zepo' instead of 'Zepho.' The Masoretic Hebrew here points the name as Zepho.

source_text: וַ/יִּהְי֥וּ בְנֵי לוֹטָ֖ן חֹרִ֣י וְ/הֵימָ֑ם וַ/אֲח֥וֹת לוֹטָ֖ן תִּמְנָֽע־׃
english_snapshot: The sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam[b][a], and Lotan’s sister was Timna.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'Hemam'; the parallel list in 1 Chronicles 1:39 reads 'Homam.'

source_text: וַ/יָּמָת֮ בַּ֣עַל חָנָ֣ן בֶּן עַכְבּוֹר֒ וַ/יִּמְלֹ֤ךְ תַּחְתָּי/ו֙ הֲדַ֔ר וְ/שֵׁ֥ם עִיר֖/וֹ פָּ֑עוּ וְ/שֵׁ֨ם אִשְׁתּ֤/וֹ מְהֵֽיטַבְאֵל֙ בַּת מַטְרֵ֔ד בַּ֖ת מֵ֥י זָהָֽב־־׃
english_snapshot: Baal-hanan son of Achbor died[a], and Hadar reigned in his place. The name of his city was Pau, and the name of his wife was Mehetabel daughter of Matred[c][b], daughter of Me-zahab.

signals.text: Hebrew: Hadar; some textual traditions and 1 Chronicles 1:50 read Hadad.

source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֗ן בֶּ֤לַע וָ/בֶ֨כֶר֙ וְ/אַשְׁבֵּ֔ל גֵּרָ֥א וְ/נַעֲמָ֖ן אֵחִ֣י וָ/רֹ֑אשׁ מֻפִּ֥ים וְ/חֻפִּ֖ים וָ/אָֽרְדְּ׃
english_snapshot: And the sons of Benjamin: Bela[a], Beker, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim[d][c][b], and Ard.

signals.text: Some parallel genealogical traditions have a variant such as “Shuppim” for “Muppim”; this translation follows the Masoretic Text here.

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֗אמֶר הִשָּֽׁבְעָ/ה֙ לִ֔/י וַ/יִּשָּׁבַ֖ע ל֑/וֹ וַ/יִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַל רֹ֥אשׁ הַ/מִּטָּֽה־׃פ
english_snapshot: He said[a], “Swear to me,” and he swore to him. Then Israel bowed himself on the head of the bed.

signals.text: Or, 'at the head of the staff.' The Hebrew consonants can be read this way, and this is the sense reflected in the Septuagint and in Hebrews 11:21.

source_text: חַכְלִילִ֥י עֵינַ֖יִם מִ/יָּ֑יִן וּ/לְבֶן שִׁנַּ֖יִם מֵ/חָלָֽב־׃פ
english_snapshot: His eyes are darker than wine[b][a], and his teeth whiter than milk.

signals.text: Or 'His eyes are red from wine' (or 'sparkling with wine'). The rare Hebrew adjective חַכְלִילִי and the preposition מִן allow a traditional reading that connects the color to wine as cause rather than comparison.
